document.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and Rajiv Gandhi, July 2, 1987
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: Gorbachev trusted Rajiv Gandhi as an intermediary on Afghanistan. Gorbachev explains 'national reconciliation' and Gandhi cautions him about dealing with tribal society. Gorbachev complains that UN negotiator Cordovez talks only about troop withdrawal, and alleges the US pressured Pakistan to keep Soviet troops in Afghanistan longer. He calls the US position 'the main obstacle' to a political settlement.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CPSU; Soviet leader

events.description: Gorbachev and Rajiv Gandhi discuss Afghanistan, national reconciliation, Pakistan and the US role.
Shevardnadze made an unannounced visit to Afghanistan, as did Kamentsev and Kryuchkov.
Group of Pakistani generals approached Soviet military attaché to say Pakistan would never allow US bases.
Gorbachev and Rajiv Gandhi converse in Moscow about Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Shevardnadze, Kamentsev and Kryuchkov made an unannounced visit to Afghanistan.
Pakistani generals appealed to the Soviet military attaché, saying Pakistan will never allow US bases.
Plans noted to extend the Afghan ceasefire by six months.
Pakistan made a concession at Geneva reducing the withdrawal term by one month.

relationships.quote: Recently E.A. Shevardnadze made an unannounced visit there, as well as Cdes. Kamentsev and Kryuchkov.

relationships.detail: The USSR supports the Afghan leadership's reconciliation line and provides assistance to the Afghans.
relationships.quote: they are carrying out the line they formulated, and which received our support

relationships.detail: The Afghan leadership seeks to protect national reconciliation from disruption by the counterrevolution/mujahideen.
relationships.quote: protect it from disruption by a counterrevolution or the mujahideen

relationships.detail: The regime invites the opposition in Pakistan and Europe to join a coalition.
relationships.quote: They are inviting the current regime’s opposition, which is in Pakistan as well as in Europe, to join them in a coalition.

relationships.detail: The regime's opposition is located in Pakistan (and Europe).
relationships.quote: the current regime’s opposition, which is in Pakistan as well as in Europe

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says India supports the line of an independent non-aligned Afghanistan, as does the USSR.
relationships.quote: received our support, and, to the best of our knowledge, your support as well.

relationships.detail: Najib is the current Afghan leader, praised for consulting tribes.
relationships.quote: This is Najib’s strong side. He actively seeks contact with various powers, tribes.

relationships.detail: Najib's leadership is contrasted with Karmal's communist slogans; current leadership replaced Karmal's.
relationships.quote: Karmal proclaimed slogans of communism, slogans that were far from the realities of Afghan society.

relationships.detail: Karmal's approach is contrasted unfavorably with Najib's more realistic policy.
relationships.quote: The current leadership looks at things more realistically.

relationships.detail: USSR provides social and economic assistance and urges Afghans to act while Soviet troops remain.
relationships.quote: In this regard we are helping the Afghans.

relationships.detail: Pakistanis seek direct contact with the USSR, including through their foreign minister.
relationships.quote: They would like to get in direct contact with us on these issues.

relationships.detail: Pakistani generals appealed to the Soviet attaché apparently with Zia's blessing.
relationships.quote: clearly not without the blessing of Zia-ul-Haq, appealed to our military attaché.

relationships.detail: Pakistani generals told the Soviet military attaché that Pakistan will never allow American bases.
relationships.quote: Pakistan will never allow American bases on its territory.

relationships.detail: India offered Pakistan a peace and friendship treaty.
relationships.quote: the peace and friendship treaty that we offered to Pakistan.

relationships.detail: Cordovez mediates the Geneva talks, focusing on troop withdrawal.
relationships.quote: all Cordovez talks about is withdrawing troops.

relationships.detail: Pakistan faced trouble from the Americans after conceding to shorten the withdrawal timetable in Geneva.
relationships.quote: when the Pakistanis made a concession in Geneva and reduced the term by just one month, they got a lot of trouble from the Americans.

relationships.detail: The US is called the main obstacle and seeks to discredit the USSR.
relationships.quote: it is the position of the United States... it allows them to discredit the Soviet Union

relationships.detail: US tension in Afghanistan is said to push Pakistan into American arms.
relationships.quote: keeping tension in Afghanistan pushes Pakistan into their arms.

sources_cited: Translation by Anna Melyakova for the National Security Archive
key_claims: Gorbachev says the Afghan leadership is pursuing national reconciliation, power-sharing and a coalition including opposition in Pakistan and Europe.
Gorbachev credits Najib with seeking contact with tribes and holding jirgas, contrasting him with Karmal.
Pakistani generals reportedly signalled via the Soviet military attaché, with Zia's blessing, that Pakistan would never allow US bases.
Gorbachev claims Pakistan was pressured by the Americans after conceding a one-month shorter withdrawal term in Geneva.
Gorbachev names the US position as the main obstacle to a political settlement.
